newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM cancels contracts amid political feud.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM cancels contracts amid political feud.

text.p: Feuding between Cambodia's ruling parties has spilled over into the business arena, with co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh declaring void major contracts signed by a rival politician.

In a letter obtained by Reuters on Friday, Ranariddh informed Ariston Sdn Bhd that the Malaysian company's deals to lease land for a large resort and an 18-hole golf course and an airport concession agreement were cancelled.
"The agreements are null and void," Ranariddh wrote in the letter, dated February 26 and addressed to Ariston Chief Executive Officer Chen Lip Keong.
The agreements, signed on September 16, were key parts of Ariston's $1.3 billion plan to develop the southern port city of Sihanoukville into a major tourist destination.

But Ranariddh said the contracts had been signed by co-Minister of the Council of Ministers Sok An, a member of co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP), without proper authorisation or notification of key officials.

Ranariddh said he was happy to receive assurances that "Ariston is apolitical and nonpartisan as stated in your (earlier) letter, but the agreements that were signed by Ariston and only (Sok An)... suggested otherwise."
Sok An would not comment on the contract or Ranariddh's cancellation of the contract.
Ariston officials were unavailable for comment.
The move by Ranariddh is likely to shake investors in Cambodia, who have long worried that tensions between Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and the CPP would undermine their businesses, analysts said.
They said they had not been swayed by conciliatory rhetoric from the two leaders earlier this week.
"High-profile deals can become very political," said one Asian diplomat.

Analysts told Reuters the problems between the two premiers, who formed a shaky coalition government following elections in 1993, would worsen as Cambodia approaches national elections, scheduled for 1998.
FUNCINPEC and CPP will oppose each other in the polls.
"Investors are very keen about future elections. They want to wait and see... (especially) with big projects," said Kwangduk Yoon, commercial attache for the Korea Trade Center.
